company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point tailwind to gross margins) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105 basis point tailwind), not operational strength. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, a market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without tariff refunds — ex-refunds EPS was 42 cents, still above consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS band of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman remaining through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The move resolves CFO uncertainty with a well-credentialed hire.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% vs. the Street's 13.85%, as management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing household budgets. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% but slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in the North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year, though the company will not provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a significant data point for the company's position in the competitive obesity and metabolic disease drug space. The strong efficacy readout is a major positive catalyst for the stock.

sectors: The RV industry faces ongoing macro headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. The GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a fresh positive data point from Viking's VK2735 trial. Cognex's RealSense deal highlights continued corporate investment in Physical AI and robotics perception.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, so there's no broad macro or Fed commentary this morning — let's go straight through the names reporting before the open.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share, coming in at $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03. But the beat was low quality — tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO adjustment added another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is less impressive. Domestic comps missed at plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027. Mixed read overall — the headline beat but the underlying fundamentals were soft.

Cognex is buying RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly $500 million upfront plus about $106 million more. RealSense is expected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic move into the Physical AI and robotics space — bullish for the longer-term thesis.

MillerKnoll is the cleanest beat of the morning. Fiscal first quarter earnings per share came in at 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents. And critically, even excluding tariff refunds, EPS was 42 cents — still a beat. Sales did miss, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed slightly while the EPS range was left unchanged. Net positive.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. Hau has prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Resolves the interim CFO overhang with a credible hire — modestly positive.

THOR Industries missed. Fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share came in at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management's tone was cautious — pointing to stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets. The company won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later this fall. Bright spots include healthy dealer inventory and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog — but the overall print was a miss with a cautious outlook. Bearish near-term.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the standout mover this morning. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported that its GLP-1 drug VK2735 delivered 22% weight loss in trial participants. That is a strong efficacy number in the highly competitive obesity drug space. Clearly bullish — watch this one at the open.

Bottom line for today: no broad market catalyst in this note, so price action will be driven by individual stock reactions. Viking is the headline mover. AutoZone's low-quality beat could see a muted or negative reaction. MillerKnoll is the cleanest fundamental story. Stay disciplined and size accordingly.
